To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the formation of a turbulent core is a generic feature of gravitational collapse, and (2) the magnetic field is strongly amplified in the kinematic dynamo regime.

(i) the thermodynamic properties of the gas have a significant impact on the structure and dynamics of the collapsing gas, (ii) the magnetic field is efficiently amplified via the turbulent dynamo in the case of Γ > 1 and via shock amplification in the case of sub-isothermal gas, and (iii) the magnetic field lines are strongly tangled in the former case and very coherent in the latter.
the formation of turbulent cores is only possible for sub-isothermal equations of state, whereas the formation of filamentary structures occurs for super-isothermal equations of states.
